definitions.NiceEligible: For every natural number p, finite list h of points in ℤ², and point z in ℤ², NiceEligible(p,h,z) means that z ≠ (0,0) and, for each point v in h with its last entry removed, z is not within coordinatewise distance p of v: at least one coordinate difference lies outside the inclusive interval [−p,p]. No condition requires h to begin at the origin or have legal consecutive jumps. For an empty or singleton h, eligibility is exactly z ≠ (0,0). For p = 0, the additional condition excludes precisely the points appearing before the last entry; the last entry itself is not tested unless it also appears earlier.
definitions.niceEligibleDecidable: For every natural number p, finite list h of integer-coordinate points, and point z, this instance supplies a decision, with evidence for the selected alternative, whether z is different from (0,0) and no point of h after removing its last entry has both coordinate differences from z in [−p,p]. It decides that proposition; it does not assert it always holds. Empty and singleton lists reduce the decision to whether z differs from the origin, and p = 0 is included.
definitions.niceReduction: For every natural number p and total devil strategy D mapping finite lists of integer-coordinate points to optional points, niceReduction(p,D) is the total strategy that, on input h, first evaluates D(Rₚ(h)). For any finite list h of integer-coordinate points, define Rₚ(h) recursively as follows: Rₚ([]) = []; if h is nonempty with last point z = (0,0), then Rₚ(h) = [(0,0)]; otherwise remove the last point to obtain q, find the least index i of q whose point differs from z by at most p in each coordinate, and, if such an index exists, set Rₚ(h) = Rₚ(q.take(i+1)) followed by z; if no such index exists, set Rₚ(h) = [z]. Indices start at zero. If this evaluation returns no point, the new strategy returns no point. If it returns z, the new strategy returns z exactly when z ≠ (0,0) and no point in h with its last entry removed is within coordinatewise distance p of z; otherwise it returns no point. The eligibility test uses the original list h. This definition includes p = 0, empty lists, and lists that are not journeys from the origin.
definitions.Allowed: For every natural number p, devil strategy D (a total function from finite lists of points in ℤ² to optional points), and finite point list h, Allowed(p,D,h) means: h is nonempty and starts at (0,0); every pair of consecutive entries has each coordinate displacement in [−p,p]; and for every pair of natural-number indices i < j and every point z, if the entry of h at index j exists and equals z, then D applied to the first i+1 entries of h does not return z. Thus every entry after index i is excluded from the single optional burn selected on that prefix, for every earlier index i. Out-of-range j impose no condition; a valid j and i < j ensure i is in range. No burn from an empty prefix is tested, and no restriction is placed on D evaluated on the whole list. The empty list is not allowed, the singleton origin list is allowed for every D and p, and p = 0 is included.

claim-2-6: For every natural number p, every total function D from finite lists of points in ℤ² to optional points, and every finite point list h, suppose h starts at (0,0), its consecutive entries differ by at most p in each coordinate, and for all indices i < j within h, the strategy E on the first i+1 entries does not return h[j]. Here E(q) evaluates D(Rₚ(q)) and returns its selected point z only if z ≠ (0,0) and z is not within coordinatewise distance p of any entry of q before its last; in every other case E(q) returns no point. For any finite list h of integer-coordinate points, define Rₚ(h) recursively as follows: Rₚ([]) = []; if h is nonempty with last point z = (0,0), then Rₚ(h) = [(0,0)]; otherwise remove the last point to obtain q, find the least index i of q whose point differs from z by at most p in each coordinate, and, if such an index exists, set Rₚ(h) = Rₚ(q.take(i+1)) followed by z; if no such index exists, set Rₚ(h) = [z]. Indices start at zero. Then Rₚ(h) starts at (0,0), has consecutive coordinate displacements in [−p,p], and for every pair of its indices i < j, D evaluated on its first i+1 entries does not return its entry at j. The assumptions exclude empty h but include the singleton origin list; p = 0 is permitted. There is no assumption that D itself satisfies any restriction on its chosen burns.
theorem-2-4: For every pair of natural numbers p and N and every devil strategy D, use the following conventions. Points are pairs of integers, and a p-jump permits a displacement in each coordinate between −p and p, inclusive, including zero displacement. A devil strategy is any total function from finite point lists to either a point or no point. An angel strategy is any total function from a finite point list and a finite list of optional points to a point. For strategies A and D, start with visited list [(0,0)] and empty burn list; at each round append D evaluated on the current visited list to the burn list, then append A evaluated on that visited list and the updated burn list to the visited list. Let xₙ denote its last point after n rounds. A round m is legal when the displacement from xₘ to xₘ₊₁ is a p-jump and the optional value representing xₘ₊₁ does not occur in the burn list after round m+1. A no-point burn forbids no point; repeated burns are permitted. Suppose that for every angel strategy A and every natural number n, if all rounds m < n of the play against D are legal, then both coordinates of xₙ belong to [−N,N]. There exists a devil strategy E such that (i) for every nonempty finite point list q starting at (0,0) with consecutive coordinate displacements in [−p,p], whenever E(q) returns z, z differs from (0,0) and is not within coordinatewise distance p of any point in q before its last; and (ii) for every angel strategy A and every natural number n, if all rounds m < n of the play against E are legal, then both coordinates of its xₙ belong to [−N,N]. E may return no point, and its values on lists failing the stated journey conditions are unrestricted. No equality or other explicit relation between E and D is required by the conclusion. Both p = 0 and N = 0 are included. At n = 0 the legal-prefix hypothesis is empty and x₀ is the origin. For later n the confinement implication imposes no requirement on a play whose first n rounds include an illegal round.
uniform-confinement: For every natural number p with p > 0, use the following conventions. Points are pairs of integers, and a p-jump permits a displacement in each coordinate between −p and p, inclusive, including zero displacement. A devil strategy is any total function from finite point lists to either a point or no point. An angel strategy is any total function from a finite point list and a finite list of optional points to a point. For strategies A and D, start with visited list [(0,0)] and empty burn list; at each round append D evaluated on the current visited list to the burn list, then append A evaluated on that visited list and the updated burn list to the visited list. Let xₙ denote its last point after n rounds. A round m is legal when the displacement from xₘ to xₘ₊₁ is a p-jump and the optional value representing xₘ₊₁ does not occur in the burn list after round m+1. A no-point burn forbids no point; repeated burns are permitted. Assume that it is not the case that there exists an angel strategy A for which every round is legal against every devil strategy D. Then there exist a natural number N > 0 and a devil strategy D such that, for every angel strategy A and every natural number n, if every round m < n in their play is legal, both coordinates of xₙ lie in [−N,N]. The same N and D must work for all A and n; they may depend on p and on the assumption. No restriction on D's choices beyond its stated function type is imposed, and no requirement that a legal play continues indefinitely appears in the conclusion. The zero-round hypothesis is vacuous and the point is the origin; if a play has an illegal round before n, this implication makes no assertion about its point at n. The hypotheses exclude p = 0 and the conclusion excludes N = 0.
